gist: England secured a valuable 3-1 first-leg win over Greece in World Cup qualifying.
Maya le Tissier scored her first international goal while making her 15th cap.
Sarina Wiegman debuted teenager Erica Meg Parkinson and handed a debut to Grace Fisk.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: England won 3-1 against Greece in Crete on Friday night during their Women's World Cup qualifying play-off first leg. Maya le Tissier scored in the 63rd minute, while Sarina Wiegman handed debuts to Erica Meg Parkinson and Grace Fisk.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The victory gives England a first-leg lead as they attempt to secure their place in Brazil next year. However, defensive lapses and a failure to keep a clean sheet left Wiegman admitting frustrations over the team's sloppiness.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: England will face Greece again in the second leg on Tuesday in Leicester to finish the job, with the winner advancing to face Ukraine or Slovakia in round two.

gist: European football features several historic clubs currently playing outside their top domestic divisions.
Criteria for inclusion involve history, heritage, fanbase, stadium capacity, and previous success.
Many of these sleeping giants have experienced financial trouble and recent ownership changes.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Several once-mighty European football clubs, such as Bursaspor, Bordeaux, and Sampdoria, have experienced severe financial difficulties, relegations, and ownership changes in recent years, leaving them competing outside their domestic top flights.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: These clubs boast rich histories, large fanbases, and significant stadium capacities. Their current struggles highlight the fragile nature of football heritage amidst financial instability.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Many of these fallen giants are under new ownership, undergoing stadium redevelopments, and attempting to climb back up their domestic football pyramids.

gist: Football Leaks founder Rui Pinto will remain in witness protection in Portugal.
Authorities suspended the decision to end his protection after a legal flaw.
Pinto released documents that triggered the Premier League investigation into Manchester City.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Authorities in Portugal suspended the decision to end Rui Pinto's witness protection programme after the Ministry of Justice stated the commission failed to adequately notify him or give him a chance to challenge the ruling. Pinto was given 10 days to assess a risk assessment.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Pinto is the Portuguese computer hacker who founded Football Leaks and released confidential documents that helped trigger the Premier League investigation into Manchester City, who were recently found guilty of breaching financial regulations.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Pinto will assess the risk assessment provided by the special security programmes commission within 10 days.

gist: JJ Gabriel features in Manchester United's official team photo despite efforts to leave.
Europe's top clubs are interested in the teenager as he holds a European Union passport.
His decision to seek a move was triggered by non-inclusion against Sabah FK.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: JJ Gabriel is included in Manchester United's official team photo for the season. The pictures were taken before he informed the club of his intention to leave. His exit decision was triggered by not being included in the squad to face Sabah FK.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Gabriel is a target for several top European clubs, including Real Madrid and Barcelona. Manchester United hold his registration and would consider legal action if illegal inducement emerges.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Gabriel is set to turn 16 and his next involvement in a United game will virtually certainly be as an opposition player.
